title: Multiplexed backpressure prober for SSE/WebSocket streaming at scale
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reusable, multi-tenant load prober that emulates realistic client backpressure and token-rate shaping for SSE and WebSocket streaming paths. The harness must produce stable tokens/sec and p95 latency signals at scale, surface regressions automatically, and be cheap to run in CI and perf labs.

Context: Existing streaming harnesses generate high-level tokenflow but do not emulate intermittent client-side backpressure (slow readers, variable recv windows) or multiplexed sessions from many tenants sharing a connection. This leads to blind spots: regressions in KV-cache interaction and kernel-scheduling under partial-read scenarios are not reproducible.

Scope: Implement a three-part system: (1) generator: client emulators that open SSE or WS connections and run configurable read/write pacing (token bursts, paused reads, slow-sink modes, variable keep-alive); (2) controller: experiment runner that orchestrates multi-tenant mixes, sequences ramp-ups, and injects chaos (simulated network jitter, TLS renegotiation); (3) collector: telemetry pipeline that exports first-byte, mid-stream p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, server error-type breakdown, and per-tenant KV-cache hit/miss correlation to Prometheus/Grafana and to a lightweight regression detector service.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generator supports: SSE and WebSocket, per-connection token shaping, prefix/KV cache warming, connection multiplexing (N logical sessions per TCP).
- Controller can define tenant profiles (burstiness, concurrency, average token length) and run reproducible scenarios. Scenario spec format stored in repo.
- Collector exports metrics with labels: protocol, tenant_id_hash, scenario, node_id. Must capture first-byte and end-of-stream times per message and aggregated tokens/sec at 1s and 30s windows.
- Regression detector: flags regressions when p95 latency increases by >15% vs baseline window (72h median) and p-value < 0.01 (Mann-Whitney U), or tokens/sec drops by >20% with correlated increase in server CPU or stall events.
- CI integration: smoke scenario on every PR that touches runtime/networking with duration <= 10m and stable gating rules.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Accuracy vs cost: 1:1 client emulation is expensive. We will multiplex logical sessions per process (configurable 4-32) and model realistic inter-message timers rather than full browser stacks. This reduces fidelity for some browser edge cases but keeps lab cost manageable.
- Statistical detection: prioritized non-parametric tests over simple thresholding to reduce false positives when workload variance is high. Baseline windows should be sliding and tagged with release.
- Observability: prefer high-cardinality labels only for short-term debug window; main dashboards aggregate across tenant cohorts to avoid cardinality blowup.

Implementation plan:
1) Week 1-2: prototype generator supporting SSE/WS with token pacing, multiplexing, and a scenario YAML spec.
2) Week 3: controller & simple ramp scheduler + chaos hooks.
3) Week 4: collector instrumentation, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboard templates.
4) Week 5: regression detector prototype and CI smoke integration.
5) Week 6: run cross-node multi-tenant soak and tune thresholds; document runbook and add an ops alerting policy.

Success criteria: reproducible p95 regressions in perf lab that match production incidents, lower mean time to detect regressions for streaming changes, and fewer false-positive alerts in nightly runs.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence), scenario catalog (repo), sample dashboards and PRs referenced below.

2025-11-20 – Priya Patel (PM): Added tenant profile examples to the project page and prioritized 'slow-reader' and 'burst-burst' profiles for initial scenarios.

2025-11-27 – Ava Chen: Prototype generator v0.1 pushed to feature branch. Basic SSE/WS connect, token shaping, and multiplexing implemented. Link to branch: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-prober/tree/feature/eng-927406.

2025-11-30 – SRE (Jamal Ortega): Ran 50k logical-session local run. Observed p95 variance spikes when multiplexing >24 per process; recommended starting default at 16 and adding an option to cap local goroutine count.

2025-12-02 – Diego Morales: Implemented metrics export. Exposing tokens_per_sec (1s window), message_first_byte_ms, message_end_ms, server_error_type, kv_cache_hit. Added labels: protocol, scenario, tenant_cohort.

2025-12-03 – Product (Priya Patel): Confirmed CI gating requirement. We will include a lightweight 5-minute smoke scenario for PRs touching runtime networking with soft-fail and hard-fail rules documented in the PR template.
